Commands left by older installs keep shadowing the new ones.

The installer (scripts/install.sh, with an identical copy in site/install.sh that must stay identical) links our commands into the first writable PATH directory, but skips any existing command it did not create itself. A link left by an earlier generation of this tool, for example `nclaude -> ~/.nebiuslink/bin/nclaude`, therefore stays in place and silently runs an old bundle. The installer must replace links and wrapper scripts left by any previous generation (their bin directories are `~/.nebiuslink/bin`, `~/.nebiusrelay/bin` and the nconnect home's `bin`), and still skip anything else.

Users who auto-update never re-run the installer, so `migrateLegacyInstall` (packages/cli/src/lib/legacy-migration.ts) must do the same on start: scan the PATH directories for symlinks that point into an older generation's bin directory and repoint them at the matching command in the new home's `bin` (the old main command `nebiusrelay` maps to `nconnect`; other names keep their name). Add an option `pathDirs?: string[]` (defaulting to the directories in PATH) and a result field `repointedLinks: string[]` holding the paths of the links that were changed. Links that are not ours are left alone. `legacyMigrationNotice` must mention it, as "Repointed N command link(s)".

This is a pnpm monorepo. Run one test file with `cd packages/tests && node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/<file>.test.ts`; do not run the whole suite. packages/cli imports @nconnect/models from its build output, so after changing packages/models run `node_modules/.bin/tsc -p packages/models/tsconfig.json` from the repository root. Dependencies are already installed: never run pnpm, npm or any install command. Do not bump versions or edit CHANGELOG or the site/ folder.
